about.title: Santa Maria Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a family in Santa Maria loses someone suddenly, the paperwork arrives long before the grief settles. A wrongful death claim is the civil path California gives surviving relatives to recover what a preventable death took from them: funeral and burial costs, the income that person would have brought home, and the love, companionship and guidance no ledger can capture. It runs separately from any criminal case. Santa Barbara County records show 7 traffic deaths in Santa Maria during 2025. Broadway, Main Street, Blosser Road and Donovan Road carry the highest collision counts in the city's public data, and reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Whatever happened, standing to sue is limited under state law, with a spouse or domestic partner and children first in line, and the deadline generally runs two years from the date of death, shorter when a government agency is involved. We handle wrongful death claims on contingency and can help you understand your family's options.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Maria Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who has standing in a wrongful death case, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out your family's position before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a city, county or state agency is involved. Acting promptly keeps those dates from slipping.

items.title: Every loss accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial expenses to the financial support your loved one provided and the companionship and guidance your family lost. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative was killed in a crash on Broadway and the driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that stands on its own, apart from anything the Santa Barbara County District Attorney pursues. The two cases can move at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. Waiting can be risky because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of the criminal timeline.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: State law puts a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first. If none exist, certain dependents and heirs may qualify. Because the rules can be tricky when families are blended or estranged, we will usually confirm standing before filing.

items.question: Does your firm charge our family anything?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free. We work on a contingency basis, meaning no attorney fee is owed unless your family recovers compensation.
